0.0.n: 見て is the て-form of 見る; いただき humbly presents the viewer’s action as a favor and connects to the thanks.

0.2.n: ありがとう combines with ございました to express polite gratitude for something already done.

0.3.n: ござい is part of ございました, which makes ありがとう more polite.

0.4.n: まし is the form of the polite ending ます used before the past ending た.

0.5.n: た completes ございました, marking the thanks as referring to the viewing already done.

1.0.n: また points to meeting another time and is common in farewells.

1.2.n: 次 connects to 動画 through の to specify which video.

1.3.n: の links 次 to 動画; English expresses this relationship simply as next video.

1.4.n: 動画 refers to the next video where the speaker expects to see viewers again.

1.5.n: で marks the video as the setting where the meeting will happen.

1.6.n: 会いましょう is the polite suggestion form of 会う, used here as a friendly farewell.

0.lit: Having received the favor of your watching, thank you.
0.tip: 見ていただき politely treats the viewer’s watching as a favor received by the speaker.

1.lit: Again, in the next video, let’s meet!
1.tip: 会いましょう literally suggests meeting, but here naturally works as see you.
